missionPremise: OPS-16 amendment A-073 (2026-09-02) added P-108. The privacy policy of a product about to take live money carries no retention section, and nine candidate routes serve the SPA shell while /privacy and /terms serve real HTML. The card's governing constraint is that retention be described AS BUILT, because terms.html previously promised a Stripe billing-portal cancellation path that existed nowhere in the app and took a blocking card (A-062) to fix. The privacy policy must not repeat that shape.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (a) curl the deployed host and get real HTML at a stable documentation URL rather than the SPA shell, (b) read every sentence of the privacy retention section back to a store, a job, or a code path named in this checkpoint, and (c) run one command that FAILS when either of those stops being true.
scopeBasis: The card names two gaps and bounds terms.html off because A-062 (PR #334) ships a check that reads it. Files touched are therefore privacy.html, a new docs.html, vercel.json (the rewrite mechanism the card's item 2 points at), and a new guard under apps/property-explorer/scripts/. Nothing in the card's bounded-off list is touched. Pricing, tier and capability claims are not changed; no carousel images; no cookie banner; no directory-listing copy.

files: 10 files, none in this lane's set

contentionCheck.intersection: EMPTY. No open PR touches public/privacy.html, public/docs.html, vercel.json, or apps/property-explorer/scripts/.
contentionCheck.vercelJsonAdjacency: P-103 (which the a062 seat note names as holding vercel.json) MERGED as #331 on 2026-08-31; origin/main 10f2a3b already carries the removal (git log --oneline origin/main -- apps/property-explorer/vercel.json shows 847550a at the top, and grep for pe-billing on origin/main returns nothing). vercel.json is free. The stale P:/tmp/hauska-map-p103-seam worktree still shows the removal as an unmerged diff only because its origin/main ref was never refetched.

storeFindingsThatGovernTheWords.method: Code read of the write paths on legacy-design-tools origin/main FIRST (ENFORCEMENT: code reading outranks output measuring), then confirmed against the live production catalog and row counts. Both are recorded; where they disagree the code read wins and the disagreement is named.

counts.countingRule: select count(*) on each table in schema public of database neondb, one query, no sampling

whatDeletes.instrument: git grep '\.delete(' on legacy-design-tools origin/main across artifacts/api-server/src/routes and .../lib, test files excluded, then the resulting target list read one by one. Exclusion set: product code outside api-server, and Map/Set .delete() calls which the same grep returns and which were separated by reading each hit.
peTablesWithADeletePath: pe_saved_properties — DELETE /property-explorer/v1/saved-properties/:parcelNodeId, propertyExplorer.ts:455, hard delete of the row scoped to (tenant, owner, parcel). Also peScreenSaveDb.ts:269.
pe_team_members and pe_team_invitations — roster management, peTeamRoster.ts:358 and :390.
users — DELETE /users/:id, users.ts:504, guarded by requireUsersManage, an admin console permission. NOT a self-serve Smart Site path.

cascadeFromUsers.derivedFrom: information_schema referential_constraints against production, not from the ORM source
cascadeFromUsers.THE_GAP: pe_saved_properties and pe_screens have NO foreign key to users at all (verified: the FK query over those two tables returns only pe_screen_rows->pe_screens). Deleting a user row therefore leaves their saved properties — which hold notes, chat threads, drawings and exports in the snapshot jsonb — and their screens in place, orphaned. gtm_events and gtm_consent likewise have no FK.
cascadeFromUsers.consequence: The privacy page may not say 'deleting your account removes your data'. It is not true today.

scheduledDeletion.pgCron: ABSENT. select extname from pg_extension returns plpgsql, postgis, vector. No pg_cron.
scheduledDeletion.triggers: ABSENT. information_schema.triggers over the pe_* tables, users, gtm_events and records_request_jobs returns 0 rows.
scheduledDeletion.scheduledWorkflows: The only .github/workflows file in legacy-design-tools carrying a cron is neon-pooler-canary.yml, which is a connectivity canary, not a retention job.
scheduledDeletion.inProcessSweeps: app.ts starts four sweeps: briefingGenerationJobsSweep (30d, keep 5 per engagement), findingRunsSweep (rescue only), terrainGenerationJobsSweep (terminal rows 30d), adapterCache. NOT ONE of them touches a pe_* table, gtm_events, or records_request_*. Verified by reading each sweep's delete target.
scheduledDeletion.conclusion: Nothing in the system deletes user data on a schedule. Any retention PERIOD written on the privacy page would be a target, not a fact.

whatDoesExpire.shareLinks: 30 days, enforced at READ, not by deletion. api/_lib/pe-share-token.ts SHARE_TOKEN_TTL_MS = 30*24*60*60*1000 bounds the HMAC token; api/_lib/pe-share-grant.ts compares Date.parse(row.expiresAt) and returns share_grant_expired. Live check: all 12 grants in pe_share_grants expire 2026-09-26..28, 0 expired, 0 revoked — so no expired row has yet existed and the persistence of expired rows is established from the absence of a delete path, not from data.
whatDoesExpire.sessionCookie: 7 days. api/_lib/session-cookie.ts SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS = 7*24*60*60*1000, and independently artifacts/api-server/src/lib/sessionToken.ts DEFAULT_TTL_SEC = 7*24*60*60 on the HMAC payload's exp. Stateless: there is no server-side session table, so signing out clears the cookie and does not revoke an already-issued token.

whatIsNotStored.cardData: No column anywhere in the production schema matches card|pan|cvv|payment_method|iban|routing (one false positive: finding_runs.discarded_finding_count). Stripe holds the payment method; we hold pe_user_entitlements.stripe_customer_id, populated on 9 of 14 rows.
whatIsNotStored.chatTranscriptsServerSide: The research-chat route (brokerageBrief.ts:1071) does not persist the message or the answer. Its only write is recordGtmEvent, and only when an installId is present — the PE web path is explicitly the no-installId branch. Confirmed in data: 49 research_chat_turn events exist and ZERO carry a pe-* install id; the payload keys are messageLength, clientTier, areaScope, visibleParcelCount — a length, never the text.
whatIsNotStored.uploadedFiles: src/workbench/tools/chat-attach.ts keeps the file client-side and injects only extracted text into the outgoing message. No upload endpoint, no blob. Caps: 10 MB per file, 5 per thread, 12,000 chars of extracted text.
whatIsNotStored.passwords: Smart Site has none. user_auth_credentials holds 14 rows for the plan-review console (routes/auth.ts) and its intersection with pe_user_identities is ZERO, verified by join. The equal count of 14 is coincidence and was checked rather than assumed.

whatIsStoredAndSurprising.searchText: gtm_events payload_json.lookupQuery holds the raw string typed into the search box on 241 events; 118 of them begin with a street number and 20 carry a state+ZIP. Keyed to an anonymous localStorage install id (src/lib/installId.ts), not to an account. No retention, no deletion path.
whatIsStoredAndSurprising.parcelPerBrowse: pe_browse_started (10,520 rows) carries parcelNodeId on every row.
whatIsStoredAndSurprising.researchContentLocation: The user's notes, chat threads, chat summary, drawings, exports and share packages live inside pe_saved_properties.snapshot. Live key inventory over 23 rows: savedAt 19, address 19, pin 11, exports 9, notes 4, chatThread 4, chatSummary 4, drawings 4, sharePackages 4, shareReportSelection 3, status 3, chatThreads 2. This is what makes 'unsave the property' a real deletion rather than a UI gesture.
whatIsStoredAndSurprising.recordsRequests: records_request_jobs stores user_id (1 distinct) and has a user_email column that is NULL on all 40 rows. records_request_artifacts holds hashed county documents; storage_path is null on all 21 today. Nothing deletes either.

defectsFoundInTheExistingPrivacyPage.severity: factual error, same class as the terms.html defect this card exists to avoid repeating
defectsFoundInTheExistingPrivacyPage.pageSays: You sign in with Google or Microsoft through WorkOS AuthKit.
defectsFoundInTheExistingPrivacyPage.truth: The workbench sign-in goes DIRECTLY to Google OIDC (fetchIdTokenClaims on the id_token) or Microsoft Graph (fetchMicrosoftProfile on the access_token), with PKCE, in apps/property-explorer/api/auth.ts. WorkOS appears in exactly one place: completeWorkOsExternalAuth in api/_lib/workos-complete.ts, reached only when pending.externalAuthId is set, which only happens when an MCP client arrives at /api/auth/mcp-login?external_auth_id=... That is the AI connector's OAuth, not the app's sign-in.
defectsFoundInTheExistingPrivacyPage.disposition: CORRECTED on privacy.html. It is a statement about where identity data goes, which is the substance of a privacy policy, and it is not a pricing, tier or capability claim, so it is not in the card's exclusion list. Flagged here because it is a change beyond the retention section.

defectsFoundInTheExistingPrivacyPage.truth: True of resolution, false of storage. The link stops resolving at 30 days; the row is never removed because nothing deletes pe_share_grants.
defectsFoundInTheExistingPrivacyPage.disposition: Made precise in the retention section rather than deleted.

docsPageDesign.route: /docs and /docs/ -> /docs.html, added to vercel.json rewrites ABOVE the /((?!api/).*) SPA catch-all, which is the same mechanism /privacy and /terms already use (and the reason both serve real HTML today).
docsPageDesign.beforeState: curl https://smartsite.cloud/docs -> 200, 1215 bytes, title 'Smart Site — Explore your property' (the SPA shell). /privacy -> 200, 5352 bytes, title 'Privacy | Smart Site'. /terms -> 200, 5074 bytes. Measured 2026-09-02.
docsPageDesign.claimsPolicy: Per-sentence provenance recorded in CP2. Every sentence traces to _smartsite_masters/ 00, 01, 05, 06, 07, 08, or to _decisions/2026-08-31_smartsite_connector_is_a_door_not_a_tier.md and _decisions/2026-09-01_mls_vendor_data_closed_as_a_source.md. Coverage is spoken of as nationwide United States with no county enumerated, per master 06 and 08.
docsPageDesign.deliberateOmission: No prices on the page. The card forbids changing any pricing claim, the ladder is locked in a doc that a static HTML file cannot track, and the in-app pricing surface is the source of truth. The page names what the free layer includes (master 06's own free-row wording) and says the deep work needs a plan, without a number. Named here so a successor can tell this from an oversight.

masterConflictRouted.conflict: Master 05 capability note says the agent door is architecture-true but not commercially live, and master 07 says commercial agent access is arranged conversation by conversation, not self-serve today. The dispatch's ground truth says the connector is a door available at every rung including Free.
masterConflictRouted.resolution: NOT a conflict once both are read. _decisions/2026-08-31_smartsite_connector_is_a_door_not_a_tier.md postdates both masters (2026-08-31 vs 08-27/08-29), rules the Smart Site MCP connector free at every rung, and explicitly separates it from agent access at programmatic volume, which is what the masters' not-commercially-live line is about. The docs page describes the connector as the subscriber's own assistant and says nothing about metered or programmatic agent access.
masterConflictRouted.leftForTheOperator: Masters 05 and 07 still read as if the connector itself were not live. That is a master-refresh item, not something this lane edits.

adversarialReview.q1_whatExecutesTheCheck: apps/property-explorer/scripts/pe-public-pages-guard.mjs, added to the property-explorer test script alongside the two guards already wired there (pe-chrome-kit-gate, seam-retired-guard).
adversarialReview.q2_whatTriggersIt: pnpm --filter property-explorer test, which the PE CI job runs on every pull request touching apps/property-explorer.
adversarialReview.q3_whatFailsAndIsItRunningToday: Non-zero exit before the vitest run, so the PR check goes red. The two sibling guards already run this way on every PE PR, so the trigger exists in production CI today rather than being added by this card.
adversarialReview.q4_whatBypassesIt: A change that does not touch apps/property-explorer (the workflow path filter). A direct push to main. A page added under a different basename that the guard's page list does not name — the list is data in the guard and adding a page without adding its entry is not caught, which is named rather than implied. And the guard reads the repository, never the deployed host, so a Vercel-side route override would not be seen.
adversarialReview.meaningShapedNotPresenceShaped: Two of the checks compare INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED values: the 30 days and 7 days in privacy.html prose against SHARE_TOKEN_TTL_MS in api/_lib/pe-share-token.ts and SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS in api/_lib/session-cookie.ts. The page author and the TypeScript constant are different sources; no sentinel satisfies both. The deletion check is the same shape in the other direction: it derives whether a self-serve account-deletion handler exists in api/ and requires the page's wording to match what it found.
adversarialReview.positiveControls: Every check also asserts something that MUST be present, so an extractor that has gone blind fails instead of reporting clean — the pattern seam-retired-guard.mjs established and the reason it is the template.
howThisCouldStillGoWrong: The guard proves the page and the code agree; it does not prove either is right. The store reading above is what makes the words true, and that is a one-time act by a fallible reader, not a mechanism.
The docs page describes the product on 2026-09-02. Nothing re-checks it against the masters. If the report menu changes, the page rots silently. Named as leave-behind rather than papered over.

The retention section says nothing deletes on a schedule. If a retention job is ever added, the page becomes WRONG IN THE SAFE DIRECTION (understating deletion), which the guard does not catch. The reverse — a promise added without a job — is what the guard's deletion check catches.
